angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 449,967 km at 83.57 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.9662 +/- 0.0150 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 83.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.646783 +/- 0.028803 solar radii from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-21 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract): 449,967 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.676023 +/- 0.067602 solar masses from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-21 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4222.06 +/- 88.15 K from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-21 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-21 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-21.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.647, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
